class.name: VoxelServer
class.brief_description: Low-level owner of all sparse signed distance field voxel data.
class.description: VoxelServer holds every voxel field in the engine behind an opaque [RID], in the same way that [RenderingServer] holds meshes and textures. It is the only place voxel data actually lives; every other voxel class is a handle to it. Most code should not use this class directly. Prefer the resource and node layers built on top of it, which manage the server's [RID]s automatically and integrate with the scene tree, the inspector, and resource saving. Every method here takes the [RID] of the field it acts on, and every position is in that field's own space. Fields are independent of one another: there is no current field, no global grid, and nothing that one field can do to another.

method.name: field_add_channel
method.description: Adds a channel of per-sample data to the field and returns its index, or the existing index if a channel of that name is already present. See [method VoxelField.add_channel].

method.name: field_clear
method.description: Empties the field without changing its bounds or voxel size.

method.name: field_create
method.description: Creates an empty field and returns its [RID]. The field must be freed with [method field_free]; nothing else will do it. Storage is not allocated until the field is first stamped into, so a created field costs almost nothing until it is used.

method.name: field_extract_island
method.description: Copies one disconnected piece of the field into a new field and returns its [RID], optionally erasing the piece from the source. The caller owns the returned field and must free it. See [method VoxelField.extract_island].

method.name: field_find_channel
method.description: Returns the index of the named channel, or [code]-1[/code] if the field has no such channel.

method.name: field_find_islands
method.description: Returns one dictionary per disconnected piece of solid in the field, largest first. See [method VoxelField.find_islands].

method.name: field_free
method.description: Frees a field and everything it owns, including the mesh [method field_get_mesh] returned. Any [RID] held for that mesh becomes invalid.

method.name: field_get_bounds
method.description: Returns the region of field space the field covers.

method.name: field_get_cell_resolution
method.description: Returns how many cells the field spans on each axis.

method.name: field_get_channel_count
method.description: Returns the number of channels, counting the material ID channel that always exists.

method.name: field_get_collision_faces
method.description: Returns the field's surface as loose triangles at the resolution set by [method field_set_collision_step]. See [method VoxelField.get_collision_faces].

method.name: field_get_mesh
method.description: Returns the [RenderingServer] mesh the field extracts into, re-extracting first if the field has changed since the last call. The [RID] is stable for the life of the field, so it can be given to [method RenderingServer.instance_set_base] once and left alone.

method.name: field_get_mesher
method.description: Returns the mesher this field extracts with.

method.name: field_get_triangle_count
method.description: Returns the number of triangles across every surface of the field's extracted mesh.

method.name: field_get_volume
method.description: Returns the volume of solid in the field, in cubic units, measured from the samples rather than from the extracted mesh.

method.name: field_get_voxel_size
method.description: Returns the distance between the field's samples.

method.name: field_is_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this [RID] refers to a field the server still owns.

method.name: field_raycast
method.description: Casts a ray through the field and returns where it first meets the surface, or an empty dictionary if it misses. See [method VoxelField.raycast].

method.name: field_sample
method.description: Returns the interpolated signed distance to the surface at a point in field space. Negative is inside the solid.

method.name: field_set_bounds
method.description: Sets the region of field space the field covers, reallocating and emptying it.

method.name: field_set_collision_step
method.description: Sets how many voxels wide one collision cell is. See [method VoxelField.set_collision_step].

method.name: field_set_mesher
method.description: Sets the mesher the field extracts with, and marks the whole field for re-extraction.

method.name: field_set_voxel_size
method.description: Sets the distance between samples, reallocating and emptying the field. This is what the field costs, so it is the number to change when memory or extraction time has to come down.

method.name: field_stamp
method.description: Applies a brush to the field at a transform in field space. Only the region the brush reaches is touched and only that region is marked for re-extraction. See [method VoxelField.stamp].

method.name: field_stamp_path
method.description: Drags a brush along a polyline in field space, spacing it from the brush's own extent so the stroke comes out continuous. See [method VoxelField.stamp_path].

method.name: get_field_count
method.description: Returns the number of voxel fields the server currently owns. Useful for leak checks, since a field that is never freed keeps its memory for the lifetime of the process.

method.name: get_monitor
method.description: Returns the current value of one of the server's counters. The same values are published to the editor's monitors tab under [code]voxel/[/code], so this is for reading them from a running project rather than for finding out what they are.

constants.constant: One byte per sample, read back as the integer that was written.
One byte per sample, read back as a value from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].
Two bytes per sample, read back as a value from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].
Four bytes per sample, stored as a float with no range limit.
Adds the brush to the field and paints its material where it added anything.
Removes the brush from the field.
Keeps only what lies inside both the brush and the field.
Averages the field towards its neighbors inside the brush, without adding or removing a shape.
Writes the brush's material where the brush overlaps existing solid, leaving the surface where it was.
How many fields the server owns. Published as [code]voxel/field_count[/code].

How many regions are waiting to be re-extracted, across every field. Published as [code]voxel/chunks_dirty[/code]. This is a backlog rather than a total, so it drops to zero as soon as something asks for a mesh. Read it straight after a stamp to see how much of the field that stamp invalidated; a number close to the whole field means a stamp is touching far more than its brush covers.
How much memory every field's samples and channels take together, in bytes. Published as [code]voxel/cpu_bytes[/code].
How long the last stamp took to apply to the samples, in microseconds, not counting re-extraction. Published as [code]voxel/stamp_usec[/code].

How long the last re-extraction took, in microseconds, counting both the meshing of the changed regions and the rebuilding of the mesh from them. Published as [code]voxel/extract_usec[/code]. This is normally the larger half of the cost of a stamp.
How many triangles every field's extracted mesh holds together. Published as [code]voxel/triangles[/code].
Represents the size of the [enum Monitor] enum.
